newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Salomon analyst confident on MFN vote for China.
newsitem.headline: Salomon analyst confident on MFN vote for China.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton's decision to renew China's Most Favoured Nation (MFN) trade status will survive opposition in Congress, a senior political analyst at Salomon Brothers Inc said on Wednesday.

But the Washington-based analyst, Michael Andrews, told reporters he predicted a close vote and said the U.S. recommendation for China to be admitted to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) would probably be delayed for a year.

Earlier this week, Clinton said he would renew the trade privileges for China for a year, but critics in Congress are expected to attack the decision, with opposition based on China's human rights record and charges of illegal campaign contributions in the last U.S. election.

Andrews said he believed MFN approval would pass by a narrow margin in the House of Representatives, but probably after a bitter debate led by conservative Republicans of the religious right, which would put a strain on Sino-American ties.

"The problem is the effect on WTO," Andrews said, adding that Clinton's opponents may then seek legislation to give Congress a role in the U.S. decision on whether to back China's membership in the trade body.
Now, the decision would be made by Clinton alone.
Citing the controversy over campaign funds, Andrews said: "The mood has become colder and I think it will take a lot longer" for Clinton to act on China's WTO membership.
China has been trying for a decade to join the successor to the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade. Demands that Beijing improve market access have delayed its entry.
